chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the obligatory sacrificial animal (Hady) when it suffers a break or damage. Can its owner sell it and use its price to acquire another sacrificial animal? He said: He should sell it, give its price in charity, and offer another sacrificial animal.
ai.seo_question: What to do with the Hajj sacrificial animal if it gets injured or sick before slaughter?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedure for a Hajj pilgrim whose sacrificial animal (Hady) becomes unfit due to injury or disease before slaughter. The ruling mandates selling the animal, donating the proceeds as charity (Sadaqah), and acquiring a replacement animal to fulfill the vow, ensuring the ritual obligation is completed despite the defect. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on maintaining the validity of the sacrifice through substitution rather than merely compensating with charity.
